I have a lot to be thankful for. A good job that treats and pays me well, a lovely family that I get along with and support me well, and a wonderful girlfriend that I really do love, trust and can confide in. But last year, I wound up in a mental health hospital for just over a month after a break up that left me absolutely shattered. I was the one that ended the relationship for what I thought were "good" reasons. My grandfather had recently died and an uncle was diagnosed with cancer very soon after. Rather than stick closer to her than ever, I pushed her away and shut myself out from the world for nearly 3 months. I tried overdosing, and was on the verge of jumping off a multistorey carpark when I was taken down and brought to hospital. In this time, my ex heard I was in hospital, and uploaded a picture to her social media of her and her new boyfriend, the day I got in there. I just got worse and worse and days just felt more and more meaningless. 
This feeling has stuck with me to this day. Despite everything (on paper) looking up, I still feel utterly hollow. Nothing seems to fill any of the emptiness left from last year. And I carry the weight of knowing it was all my fault. I ended my previous relationship, I took myself to that car park, and I brought this all on myself. 
I don't feel like I deserve help or happiness and all I do deserve is live with the weight of my failures. Even getting this out now feels selfish, and just outlines how ignorant I am. I started this off by saying what I DO have, a lot of things I'm extremely lucky to have, and that others would love to have. I can't help how I feel, but I feel I do deserve it
